title: Sequential Outlier Detection in Non-Stationary Time Series
summary: The paper addresses sequential outlier detection in time series whose mean can drift, where repeated tests inflate false-positive probabilities. It estimates the mean with a one-sided local-linear smoother plus Jackknife bias reduction, then uses extreme-value theory to set GEV-based critical values for the maximum residual over n consecutive tests. In simulations and Australian temperature data, the full and partial procedures achieve high specificity and competitive sensitivity, with the full IID μ1 n=50 standard-normal setting reporting 98.3% specificity.

match_target.why: Cheapest central result and exactly matches the user's hint: it is one simulation cell for the proposed full method with no contamination, so it isolates specificity and needs only CPU. It reports the paper's headline finite-sample specificity for the target configuration.

tolerance.why: Rule 2: this is an accuracy-like % metric evaluated over 1,000 series × 550 time points (well over 2,000 observations), and the paper prints it as a percentage.

requirements.stmt: Model the observed series as Xi = μ(i/n)+ε_i+c_i, with c_i=0 for normal observations and c_i≠0 for outliers.
requirements.quote: and ci is a sequence of variables indicating a normal observation, for ci = 0, or an outlier, for ci̸ = 0.

requirements.stmt: Use one-sided local linear regression with a kernel supported on [−1,0] so that no future observations enter the estimator.
requirements.quote: In the following, we assume that K has the support [−1, 0], which means that ˆμhn(t) only depends on observations of time points i ≤nt

requirements.stmt: Apply Jackknife bias reduction to define tilde μ_n(t)=2 hat μ_{h_n/√2}(t)−hat μ_{h_n}(t).
requirements.quote: To account for the bias of this estimator, we employ the Jackknife bias reduction technique

requirements.stmt: Reject the null at time i when |Xi−tilde μ_n(i/n)| exceeds the GEV (1−α_i) quantile of estimated θ_n.
requirements.quote: Generally, we propose to reject H(i) 0 , if |Xi − ̃μn( i n)| > q1−αi(ˆθn).

requirements.stmt: Estimate the GEV parameters θ_n from the initial outlier-free period, using MLE or PWM as permitted by the paper.
requirements.quote: Different approaches exist to approximate the unknown values of θn, such as maximum likelihood estimation or the probability weighted moment (PWM) method.

requirements.stmt: Require the first n observations to be outlier-free and use them to estimate θ_n.
requirements.quote: The first observations X1, . . . , Xn do not contain outliers, i. e., ci = 0 for i = 1, . . . , n.

requirements.stmt: With constant α_i=α, the procedure has asymptotic level α for n consecutive tests.
requirements.quote: With constant level αi = α, the decision rule in (5) has asymptotic level α for n consecutive tests

requirements.stmt: Use the one-sided quartic kernel K(x)=15/8(1−x^2)^2 supported on [−1,0] in the simulation study.
requirements.quote: we selected the one-sided quartic kernel K(x) = 15 8 (1 −x2)2 with support on [−1, 0]

requirements.stmt: Tune the bandwidth by 5-fold cross-validation minimizing the mean squared error.
requirements.quote: tuned the bandwidth with 5-fold cross validation, minimizing the mean squared error.

requirements.stmt: Set the joint level α for n consecutive tests to 1% in the experiments.
requirements.quote: Finally, the joint level α for n consecutive tests was set to 1%.

requirements.stmt: Add outliers randomly to 5% of observations in the contaminated simulation setting.
requirements.quote: outliers were randomly added to the original time series at 5% of the observations.

requirements.stmt: Generate 1,000 time series with outliers and 1,000 without outliers for each simulation combination.
requirements.quote: we generated 1 000 time series with outliers and another 1 000 time series without outliers.

requirements.stmt: Define 'Ours (full)' as using the estimator based on all observations until time i.
requirements.quote: the estimator ̃μn( i n) is based on all observations until time i and refer to it as the “full” version.

requirements.stmt: Rescale the error process to mean 0 and standard deviation 1/20 whenever the variance exists.
requirements.quote: we rescaled ε to have mean 0 and standard deviation 1 20, in all cases where the variance exists.

requirements.stmt: For the real temperature data, use n=365 as the initial outlier-free year and α=1%.
requirements.quote: we set n = 365, which corresponds to an initial year without outliers, and chose α = 1%, as before.
